Yes: [1] directly addresses removing brand language from LLM text while preserving general utility, including neutralizing characteristic language, slogans, and stylistic markers. [1] is the closest match and is specifically framed as LLM Unbranding, with an inference-time method that aims to eliminate brand leakage without harming general capabilities.

[2] and [8] are related but broader: they focus on domain-agnostic redaction and policy-conditioned redaction of sensitive information while preserving semantics, not specifically company trademarks or slogans. [4], [6], and [7] also preserve utility while removing or mitigating sensitive or copyrighted content, but they do not focus on branded text or slogans.
